citation.title: Robust Bayesian Estimation for the Linear Model and Robustifying the Kalman Filter
citation.authors: C. Johan Masreliez; R. Douglas Martin

topic: Robust (heavy-tailed noise) Bayesian estimation for the linear model, and a robustified Kalman filter that uses bounded influence functions on innovations.
own_question: How can a linear Gaussian Bayesian or Kalman estimate stay efficient when either the observation noise or the state noise is symmetric and heavy-tailed?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper derives min-max influence-function estimators and covariance bounds (Theorems 1-4). It assumes a Gaussian state prediction error, which the authors acknowledge is approximate. Evidence comes from scalar examples and a one-dimensional simulated Monte Carlo study (10 steps, 1000 runs). There is no plasma, diagnostic, or real data.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: For background only: robust Kalman-type filters bound the influence of outlying innovations to limit sensitivity to heavy-tailed observation noise.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Sec. I and Sec. IV, Theorem 3, eqs. (17)-(21), pp. 362, 367-368
claim_checks.qualification: Shown under the authors' assumptions and in simulated 1-D cases only. This is a concept we cite; our study did not implement it.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. These are generic sequential state estimates, not report nowcasting.
validation_if_relevant: Simulation only, with a 1-D model and Gaussian-mixture observation noise.
forbidden_inferences: Do not imply our estimators use robust influence functions or that robustness was tested on CES labels.
Do not transfer its simulated efficiency figures to KSTAR data.
Do not cite it as evidence about plasma diagnostics or CES label noise.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation only if the theory section discusses robustness to outlier CES reports. It is otherwise not needed.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
